title: Incorrect Loop Boundary
cause: The loop stops before processing the last element due to len(numbers) - 1.
correction: Change 'range(len(numbers) - 1)' to 'range(len(numbers))' or iterate directly with 'for n in numbers:'.
hint: Check the upper limit of the range function.

title: Unterminated Statement
cause: The variable declaration statement is missing a terminating semicolon.
correction: Add a semicolon ';' at the end of line 4: 'int count = 10;'
hint: In C, every statement must end with a delimiter.

title: Mismatched Braces Scope
cause: The class body is missing a closing curly brace '}'. Only the main method was closed.
correction: Add a closing curly brace '}' for the class scope at the end.
hint: Count the open '{' and close '}' curly braces.

title: Missing Colon in Header
code:
def check_positive(num):
    if num > 0
        return "Positive"
    return "Non-positive"

print(check_positive(5))
cause: The if statement is missing a trailing colon (:).
correction: Add a colon ':' at the end of line 2: 'if num > 0:'
hint: Python control statements require a colon at the end of the line.

title: Format Specifier Mismatch
cause: Using '%d' integer format specifier to print a floating-point variable produces garbled output.
correction: Use '%f' (or '%.1f') format specifier instead of '%d'.
hint: Look at the format specifier used in printf.

title: String Equality Comparison
cause: Using '==' on Strings compares object memory references rather than string contents.
correction: Use 'a.equals(b)' instead of 'a == b'.
hint: In Java, '==' checks reference equality for objects.

title: Default Mutable Parameter Trap
code:
def append_item(val, container=[]):
    container.append(val)
    return container

append_item(10)
print(append_item(20))
cause: Default list parameter 'container=[]' is instantiated once at function definition and shared across calls.
correction: Set default to 'container=None' and initialize 'if container is None: container = []' inside function.
hint: Default arguments in Python are evaluated once when the function is defined.

title: Off-by-One Array Out of Bounds
cause: Loop condition 'i <= 5' accesses arr[5], which is out of bounds for an array of size 5 (indices 0 to 4).
correction: Change loop condition from 'i <= 5' to 'i < 5'.
hint: Array indices are 0-indexed; an array of size 5 has valid indices 0 to 4.

title: Integer Division Loss of Precision
cause: Both 'total' and 'count' are integers, so integer division truncates 100/8 to 12 before casting to double.
correction: Cast one of the operands to double: 'double avg = (double) total / count;'
hint: Dividing two integers in Java results in integer truncation before assignment.

title: Type Mismatch on User Input
code:
def double_value(user_val):
    return user_val * 2

# User enters numeric string '15'
result = double_value("15")
print(result)
cause: Multiplying a string by 2 duplicates the string ("1515") instead of performing arithmetic.
correction: Convert the input to integer: 'int(user_val) * 2'.
hint: String multiplication in Python repeats the text.

title: Missing Pointer Dereference in Scanf
cause: scanf expects the address of the variable (&age), but passing 'age' value 0 causes a segmentation fault writing to address NULL.
correction: Pass the address of age: 'scanf("%d", &age);'
hint: scanf requires pointers to memory locations where input should be stored.

title: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
cause: Accessing index 3 of an array of length 3 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
correction: Access index 2 to read the last element: 'nums[2]'.
hint: The maximum valid index for an array of length 3 is 2.

title: Variable Shadowing in List Comprehension
code:
multiplier = 10
items = [1, 2, 3]
result = [item * multiplier for item in items for multiplier in [2]]
print(result)
cause: Inner loop variable 'for multiplier in [2]' shadows the outer variable 'multiplier = 10', multiplying by 2 instead.
correction: Remove the inner comprehension loop: '[item * multiplier for item in items]'.
hint: Check the variable names in the nested comprehension.

title: Missing Break in Switch Statement
cause: Missing 'break;' statement in case 0 causes fallthrough into case 1 and default.
correction: Add 'break;' statement after 'printf("SUCCESS ");'.
hint: Cases in C switch statements fall through unless explicitly terminated.

title: NullPointerException on Uninitialized Array Element
cause: Elements of a new String array default to null. Calling '.toUpperCase()' on null throws NullPointerException.
correction: Initialize array elements with valid strings before calling methods: 'names[0] = "Alice";'.
hint: Objects in newly created arrays in Java default to null.

title: Dictionary Key Mutation
cause: Attempting attribute assignment 'scores.student' on a dictionary raises AttributeError.
correction: Use dictionary key indexing: 'scores[student] = val'.
hint: Python dictionaries use subscript square-bracket syntax for keys.

title: Dangling Pointer Return
cause: Returning a pointer to a local stack variable that is deallocated when get_counter returns.
correction: Make the variable static: 'static int count = 42;' or dynamically allocate with malloc.
hint: Local variables on the stack cease to exist once the function scope exits.

title: Infinite Recursion StackOverflowError
cause: Missing base case (e.g. if n <= 1 return 1) causes endless recursive calls until StackOverflowError.
correction: Add base case: 'if (n <= 1) return 1;' at the start of factorial.
hint: Every recursive function must have a terminating base condition.

title: Generator Exhaustion Trap
code:
def get_nums():
    yield from [1, 2, 3]

gen = get_nums()
sum_first = sum(gen)
count = len(list(gen))
print(sum_first, count)
cause: Generators in Python can only be consumed once. 'sum(gen)' exhausts it, leaving 'list(gen)' empty with length 0.
correction: Materialize the generator into a list first: 'items = list(get_nums())', then compute sum and length from items.
hint: A generator is an iterator that cannot be re-iterated once exhausted.

title: String Literal Buffer Overwrite
cause: String literal "Hello" is allocated in read-only text segment. Writing to it causes a segmentation fault.
correction: Declare str as a mutable char array: 'char str[] = "Hello";'.
hint: Pointers to string literals in C point to read-only memory.

title: Static vs Instance Field Collision
cause: 'count' is declared static, so it is shared across all Counter instances instead of being instance-specific.
correction: Remove 'static' keyword from 'count' declaration: 'public int count = 0;'.
hint: Static members belong to the class rather than individual instances.

title: Exception Swallowing Without Reraise
cause: 'pass' in the except block causes parse_int to implicitly return None, and 'None + 5' raises TypeError.
correction: Return a default value (e.g. 0) in the except block: 'return 0'.
hint: A function that falls off the end without return produces None.

title: Strcpy Destination Buffer Overflow
cause: Destination array 'small' only has capacity for 4 bytes, copying 17 bytes corrupts adjacent memory.
correction: Increase buffer size: 'char small[32];' or use strncpy: 'strncpy(small, "IEEE", 4); small[3] = '\0';'.
hint: The destination buffer must be large enough to hold the source string plus null terminator.

title: ConcurrentModificationException
cause: Modifying a collection directly while iterating over it with an enhanced for-loop throws ConcurrentModificationException.
correction: Use an explicit Iterator: 'Iterator<String> it = list.iterator(); ... it.remove();' or 'list.removeIf(item -> item.equals("B"));'.
hint: Do not structurally modify collections during enhanced for-loop iterations.

title: Shallow Copy Mutation Hazard
cause: Shallow copy copies outer list references, so nested lists remain shared between m1 and m2.
correction: Use 'copy.deepcopy(matrix)' instead of shallow copy.
hint: Shallow copy only duplicates the outer container, not nested mutable objects.

title: Integer Overflow with Signed Types
cause: Adding 1 to INT_MAX causes 32-bit signed integer overflow into negative numbers (INT_MIN).
correction: Use 64-bit integer type: 'long long next = (long long)max_val + 1;'.
hint: INT_MAX is the upper bound for signed 32-bit integers.

title: Floating Point Comparison Precision
cause: Binary floating-point representation causes 0.1 + 0.2 to evaluate to 0.30000000000000004.
correction: Compare with an epsilon tolerance: 'Math.abs(val - 0.3) < 1e-9'.
hint: Never compare floating-point arithmetic results using exact equality '=='.

title: Late Binding Closures in Loops
code:
funcs = []
for i in range(3):
    funcs.append(lambda: i)

results = [f() for f in funcs]
print(results)
cause: Python closures bind variables late, so all lambdas look up 'i' at call time when it has value 2.
correction: Bind the loop variable immediately as a default argument: 'lambda i=i: i'.
hint: Lambdas inside loops look up variables dynamically when called.

title: Memory Leak in Dynamic Allocation Loop
cause: In each iteration, ptr is reassigned without freeing previously allocated blocks, leaking 2 memory buffers.
correction: Free previous allocation before reassigning or allocate once outside the loop.
hint: Every call to malloc should have a corresponding free call.

title: Autoboxing Null Pointer Dereference
cause: Autounboxing a null Integer wrapper to primitive int invokes '.intValue()' on null, throwing NullPointerException.
correction: Check for null before unboxing or initialize box with a default integer: 'Integer box = 0;'.
hint: Unboxing a null wrapper object causes NullPointerException.
